Clawback Audits

By: Joy Summers | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Is Discovery Health playing Judge, Jury and executioner as it claw backs millions from Physiotherapists using bullying tactics.

Unique Selling Point:
UNIQUE SELLING POINTS
A great case study willing to speak out – A David and Goliath battle, a company abusing its market dominance and both a detailed actuarial investigation and a recent investigation and report written by Senior Council Les Morrison who suggests that not only is Discovery Health acting unethically, it may also be acting unlawfully, and he recommends a Constitutional Court challenge by SASP- the SA Society of Physiotherapists. His views are confirmed by Professor Birgit Kushke – an insurance law specialist at the University of Pretoria who is also ready to appear on camera. Hopefully a hard hitting interview with Discovery Health


Summary:
Terrified physiotherapists have been the subject of claw back audits by Discovery Health – several years after they have billed their clients. They say Discovery bullies them into signing acknowledgement of debt letters - implying they are unethical and dishonest, and threaten to withhold any further current payments to them unless they co-operate.
Many have remained silent – fearing the stigma of Discovery’s accusations. But in April last year when Physiotherapist Karen Gibb’s husband was slapped with a million rand audit. She closed up her own practice for six months, determined to investigate what she believed was Discovery’s unethical practice. She pierced through a veil of fear – found 43 physio’s prepared to relate their experiences to the board and a senior council. Their stories and Karen’s determination changed the board and the structure of their industry body and may well end in a Constitutional court challenge. Discovery have continued to use their tactics which they say are supported in law and protect the scheme.



Further information:
Further Information
Discovery Health say they have 3660 physiotherapists on its books and has paid out R1.8 billion rand to them between 2012 and 2020. A claw back is money paid to the practitioner and then later clawed back from them. The law says it should happen within 30 days.
Discovery health can take three years. The physio’s say they are targeted out of the blue, press ganged into signing an acknowledgement of debt and made to produce clinical notes long after the treatment has occurred. They also say that once the audit starts there is a presumption that the physio is a fraudster and Discovery Health’s forensic unit are rude and aggressive. The impact of this imputation of this dishonesty on the physio is enormous. Some have closed down their practices and left the country, others have been suicidal.

It all begins with the codes that physio’s must use as a representation of the particular treatment they administer. A machine kicks out ‘outliers’ and from there Discovery forensic unit takes over. According to Senior council Les Morrison, these physio’s find themselves in a dystopian reality where the machine determines their guilt and nothing they can say seems to make any difference to Discovery Health’s forensic unit. He says this scenario has no place in a Constitutional democracy.
Discovery argue that their claw back audits keep practitioners billing honestly and our medical aid premiums would be 14% higher. Discovery do not believe that the onus to prove the wrong doing rests with them and there is nothing of substance to complain about if the healthcare provider is actually innocent. They rely on Section 59 of the Medical schemes act and they say there is no imbalance of power in the negotiation between themselves and the physio. But that is not really true because if the physio’s don’t co-operate or disagree, then Discovery with-hold the current payments due to physio’s. Many settle simply because they cannot afford to hold out against the Medical Aid giant.

FINAL SCRIPT CLAW BACK AUDITS FOR TX 25th JULY 2021
FACT CHECKED FOR VOICE OVER

Commentary One
Many of our physiotherapists are playing a critical role right now,
helping Covid patients recover. But some of them, are living in fear.

Up sound Backslaps

Apart from the virus, it’s Discovery Health’s claw back audits, that make them tremble.
These are huge sums of money that its forensic unit says have been billed incorrectly and must be repaid, long after the patient consultation

Debbie
We are not thieves. We are well, meaning human beings that are running our businesses

Commentary Two
In 2017 Debbie Cohen’s practice was audited by Discovery Health

Debbie
You feel like a criminal. I can tell you from an emotional point of view it destroyed me.

Commentary Three
But Medical schemes are unapologetic about these audits. CEO of Discovery Health, Dr Ryan Noach says without them, the schemes they administer, would lose R1.7 billion rand per year.

Ryan Individual member contributions would be about 14 % higher per member per month in the absence of any fraud, waste and abuse management.

LINK
That the medical schemes are battling massive fraud is not in question, but is Discovery Health in particular, tarring honest medical practitioners who have made coding errors, with the same brush as the real fraudsters?

Commentary Four
Different codes are used by medical practitioners to represent specific procedures. For example, this spinal mobilization has a 401 code submitted by physiotherapists for payment to the schemes. But we are told that the codes can be complex and often ambiguous.

Derek
Ryan, how do you make a distinction between real fraudsters and medical practitioners who've made honest coding errors?
Ryan
ya the majority of the time, it is actually honest coding errors ,and each and every case is carefully looked at


Commentary Five
Cohen alleges their forensic unit was an aggressive bully

Debbie
You are ambushed. You actually ambushed. The detail looked like gibberish. It’s this spreadsheet of hundreds of thousands of lines. It wasn't understandable, certainly not to me.

Commentary six
To help her, Cohen enlisted the help of a forensic actuary. Discovery initially said she owed them over a million rand. At most, said the actuary, she owed R146 000.

Debbie
They just ignored him. They just they would not listen to him.
Derek
Debbie, you admit that you made mistakes with the Codes?
Debbie
Yes, I made mistakes with the codes, but there was no financial impact to the mistakes,
it had no monetary value. I still did the treatment

Commentary seven
In the end she settled.

Derek
Why did you settle with them if you felt that was just a mistake for the codes and they weren't any financial implications?
Debbie
They cut off my payments.
Derek
So you were getting no income.
Debbie
No income

Commentary Eight
Karen Gibbs is a sports physio, and has worked with both local and international elite athletes. She believes Discovery cuts off a practitioners income, to force them into acknowledging an unproven debt

Derek
Do some throw in the towel?
Karen
Everybody throws in the towel. I think that's critical to understand. We all capitulate at the end because of the amount of leverage. There's no physio that decides to settle because they feel they're guilty, they settle because they have no choice. Financially, they can no longer continue to fight this, Discovery’s resources are so vast.


Derek
Are you saying that Discovery doesn't always prove its case?
Karen:
I would suggest that Discovery very rarely proves its case.
Derek
Really?
Yes

Ryan
That's absolutely incorrect, Derek. And on every single case, we are prepared to account for exactly the claims that are recovered.

Commentary nine
In early 2020 Gibb’s husband, also a physiotherapist, received an audit notification. Soon after, Discovery Health suspended payments to his practice.

Karen
And then we were handed this almost arbitrary amount of money that that that we had to pay back without any concrete evidence as to how Discovery had arrived at this massive sum of money.
Derek
Can I ask how much?
Karen
The amount was in the region of about R580 000, when we disputed it quite strongly, Discovery then came back with a very thinly veiled threat, that if we did not settle for the R580 000, the amount would escalate to the region of R1.2 million.

Commentary Ten
They settled on just over R100 000

Karen
And I think that highlights the complete, almost illogical way in how these amounts are calculated R 580 000, R1,2 -settle for R100 000.

Derek
Now, when the physios say this is an unfair practice, Discovery cuts off the flow of funds, throttling their practice and forcing them to capitulate?
Ryan
No, Derek, that's a twisting of the facts. In some scenarios, the physiotherapists refuse to engage whatsoever. They refuse to provide any evidence that a suitable treatment was administered. They refused to engage in the facts of the process

Commentary eleven
Outraged by what she viewed as Discovery Health targeting innocent practitioners, Gibbs scaled back her practice for 6 months and began an investigation.


Karen
And then it turned into a bit of a crusade, because I could not believe what I was hearing from all of these physios.

Commentary Twelve
Tip off’s and an algorithm alert Discovery Health to what they call outliers.

Birgit Kuschke
One cannot claw back on an assumption produced by an algorithm.

Commentary thirteen
Professor Birgit Kuschke specialises in insurance law. In 2020 her own physiotherapist was invited by the forensic unit to a coding meeting which she attended. She was appalled when Discovery Health began a clawback two days later, without proving their claim

Birgit
They are the prosecutor, the judge, jury and executioner. Once they identify an outlier, there is an immediate acceptance that this person or this practitioner is guilty and therefore there must be a clawback, and the clawback is immediately started
Derek
Let me make this simple. You're saying that Discovery Health is not following due process?
Professor Kuschke
Yes, this is the problem, due process would allow people to defend themselves and to reach a point of legal certainty. But because this is not done, there is some form of intimidation, the practitioner signs the acknowledgement in the hope he can continue with the practice

Commentary fourteen
In 2018 at a Fraud waste and abuse summit, Discovery Health’s forensic unit put up this slide. It reveals amounts Discovery Health have clawed back from different medical practitioners. Close to 11% of physio’s were audited. Noach believes the numbers are negligeable

Derek
Ryan, Physiotherapists and the legal practitioners allege, and I quote,” that your forensic unit is a bully; refuses to engage; believes it is always right, and presumes practitioners are guilty.”
Ryan
Yeah, it makes me very sad to hear that, Derek. You know, of 3280 physio practices that billed us in 2020, less than five % were investigated for any kind of fraud, waste and abuse whatsoever
Derek
Ryan, so are you saying that the forensic unit is fair and following due process?
Ryan
Yes, the forensic unit in our perspective is definitely fair and are definitely following due process. The question on due process is unequivocal in our view we have had all sorts of legal review of the forensics activities.

Derek
A professor of law suggests otherwise. And she says the Discovery health was playing the judge, the jury and the executioner.
Ryan
Yes, we've met with Professor Kushka on numerous occasions. We have a disagreement of opinion with her and our lawyers and our external lawyers also disagreed with Prof. Kushka.

Commentary fifteen
Kuschke also believes that Discovery Health is ignoring regulation 6 which gives schemes only 30 days to flag a complaint

Birgit
Trying to investigate a case three years down the line is extremely difficult. And that is why Regulation 6 is there.

Derek
Ryan the big factor is that Discovery Health doesn't stick to the 30 day rule of regulation Six to query a bill?
Ryan
Derek, you're misunderstanding and misquoting that rule. The 30 day rule does not relate in any way to the recovery of monies that have been paid incorrectly by the medical scheme.
and section 59(3)of the Medical Schemes Act gives us every right to recover the monies that are paid illegitimately in either an error in the billing or some worse malicious situation where the billing has been fraudulent.

Commentary sixteen
Meanwhile Gibbs continued her investigation in 2020, speaking to around 70 physiotherapists. Many were afraid. Her findings led to a shake up of their professional society and an investigation by senior counsel, Les Morrison.

Karen
So what the Morrison report for me was very powerful was that it almost it validated to the physios that they were not criminals, that they were not fraudsters, that the method in which these audits had been conducted was not fair.

Commentary seventeen
Morison’s in depth report found that: “These audits as they are conducted are one-sided ‘negotiations’ only and the trend of the negotiations is going to inevitably favour the administrator. It simply is not just and must be legally addressed.

Commentary eighteen
We had many questions for Noach, but he didn’t give us a lot of time. So we asked what we could


Derek
Is the forensic team given any financial incentives for its staff to reach certain targets?
Ryan
No financial incentives at all Derek. Their performance is measured, but they are not given any targets against which they receive personal income whatsoever. We think that would be wrong.
Derek
But they are given incentives?
Ryan
They are given incentives as are all our employees, but for clarity no incentive is linked to the quantity of money that they recover but Derek I am unfortunately now out of time..
Derek
The former CEO states clearly that targets are set and they are incentives.
Ryan We've changed that, Derek, there are no incentives linked to the targets that forensic teams recover
Derek
Because this would skew the picture and explain a lot of these problems
Ryan
I don’t agree with you
Derek
Can I ask you one more question?
Ryan
I am unfortunately out of time – cheers.

Commentary nineteen
But could it be that Discovery Health’s forensic process as it stands, is also out of time? Because it’s not just physiotherapists that believe these claw back audits are unfair and unlawful. A group of highly specialised medical practitioners is considering legal action to challenge the rule that Discovery relies on, for its claw back audits.

Debbie
They threaten you, that it can happen again. I can't tell you how many patients I will treat for nothing because I can't figure out how they would want me to bill..
Derek
What would you do if they come after you again?
Debbie
I am coming back to you!
Derek
Silly laugh
Debbie
I close shop. I close shop

THE END 12:01





PROMO ONE 11 SECONDS
Fraudulent medical claims threaten the viability of Medical Schemes, so their forensic units are hard at work, but are they targeting innocent practitioners instead?

PROMO TWO 21 SECONDS
Claw back audits from medical aid schemes strike fear into the hearts of innocent medical practitioners at the mercy of a big corporate with deep pockets
Karen
We all capitulate at the end because of the amount of leverage.
Debbie
We are not thieves! We are well meaning human beings running our businesses.

PROMO THREE 21 SECONDS
Commentary
A sports physiotherapist scales back her practice for six months to investigate claw back audits she believed were unfair and targeting innocent practitioners. Now she is tackling the medical schemes head on, but they’re fighting back

Karen
And then it turned into a bit of a crusade, because I could not believe what I was hearing from all of these physios.

metadata.Unique Selling Point: UNIQUE SELLING POINTS A great case study willing to speak out – A David and Goliath battle, a company abusing its market dominance and both a detailed actuarial investigation and a recent investigation and report written by Senior Council Les Morrison who suggests that not only is Discovery Health acting unethically, it may also be acting unlawfully, and he recommends a Constitutional Court challenge by SASP- the SA Society of Physiotherapists. His views are confirmed by Professor Birgit Kushke – an insurance law specialist at the University of Pretoria who is also ready to appear on camera. Hopefully a hard hitting interview with Discovery Health
metadata.Summary: Terrified physiotherapists have been the subject of claw back audits by Discovery Health – several years after they have billed their clients. They say Discovery bullies them into signing acknowledgement of debt letters - implying they are unethical and dishonest, and threaten to withhold any further current payments to them unless they co-operate. Many have remained silent – fearing the stigma of Discovery’s accusations. But in April last year when Physiotherapist Karen Gibb’s husband was slapped with a million rand audit. She closed up her own practice for six months, determined to investigate what she believed was Discovery’s unethical practice. She pierced through a veil of fear – found 43 physio’s prepared to relate their experiences to the board and a senior council. Their stories and Karen’s determination changed the board and the structure of their industry body and may well end in a Constitutional court challenge. Discovery have continued to use their tactics which they say are supported in law and protect the scheme.
metadata.Further information: Further Information Discovery Health say they have 3660 physiotherapists on its books and has paid out R1.8 billion rand to them between 2012 and 2020. A claw back is money paid to the practitioner and then later clawed back from them. The law says it should happen within 30 days. Discovery health can take three years. The physio’s say they are targeted out of the blue, press ganged into signing an acknowledgement of debt and made to produce clinical notes long after the treatment has occurred. They also say that once the audit starts there is a presumption that the physio is a fraudster and Discovery Health’s forensic unit are rude and aggressive. The impact of this imputation of this dishonesty on the physio is enormous. Some have closed down their practices and left the country, others have been suicidal. It all begins with the codes that physio’s must use as a representation of the particular treatment they administer. A machine kicks out ‘outliers’ and from there Discovery forensic unit takes over. According to Senior council Les Morrison, these physio’s find themselves in a dystopian reality where the machine determines their guilt and nothing they can say seems to make any difference to Discovery Health’s forensic unit. He says this scenario has no place in a Constitutional democracy. Discovery argue that their claw back audits keep practitioners billing honestly and our medical aid premiums would be 14% higher. Discovery do not believe that the onus to prove the wrong doing rests with them and there is nothing of substance to complain about if the healthcare provider is actually innocent. They rely on Section 59 of the Medical schemes act and they say there is no imbalance of power in the negotiation between themselves and the physio. But that is not really true because if the physio’s don’t co-operate or disagree, then Discovery with-hold the current payments due to physio’s. Many settle simply because they cannot afford to hold out against the Medical Aid giant.
